explanations.answer: He goes out to mourn and weep for her
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Sarah dies in Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, and "Abraham went out to mourn and to weep for her." (Genesis 23:2) He doesn't rush past it or act like he's fine. I think a man who lost his wife of all those years is allowed every one of those tears.

explanations.answer: He leaves the land of Canaan for good
explanations.explanation: Not this one, friend. Abraham stays in Canaan, and the very next thing he does is talk to the Hittites about land right there (Genesis 23:3-4). The text says he went out to mourn and to weep for her (Genesis 23:2). Nobody is packing a suitcase in this scene.

explanations.answer: He sends word to his son Isaac
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd think so, since Isaac is Abraham's son. But this passage never says Abraham sends word to anybody. What it says is that he "went out to mourn and to weep for her." (Genesis 23:2) Sometimes the story just stops and lets a man cry.

Right on the money, baker. Abraham says, "Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead." (Genesis 23:4) He's a foreigner and an outsider there, so he has to ask. He doesn't own a single patch of ground to lay Sarah in.

Close to the sort of thing a traveler might ask for, friend, but not what he says here. Abraham asks for a burial site, not grazing land (Genesis 23:4). Sarah has just died, so his mind is on laying her to rest. Sheep can wait.

Good guess if you were picturing a man haggling at a market, and he does end up doing some of that. But his actual request is for a burial site (Genesis 23:4). He needs a place to bury his dead, not a spot to set up shop.

Yes, baker. The Hittites tell him, "Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead." (Genesis 23:6) That's a generous answer to a man who just called himself an outsider. Nobody shuts a door on him.

Not quite, friend. The Hittites say the opposite of holding back. They tell Abraham, "None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead." (Genesis 23:6) So every one of them is saying yes, and they even offer the finest tombs.

explanations.answer: He rises and bows down before them
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. "Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites." (Genesis 23:7) They had just called him God's chosen one, and he answers by bowing low. I think that's a man who doesn't let a compliment go to his head.

explanations.answer: He turns down any help from them
explanations.explanation: Not here, friend. Abraham doesn't wave them off. He rises, bows down, and then asks them to approach Ephron on his behalf (Genesis 23:7-8). A man who needs a favor and says thank you with a bow is no help-refuser.

explanations.answer: He leaves to look for land elsewhere
explanations.explanation: Nope, he stays put. The Hittites just offered him their finest tombs, so he has no reason to go anywhere (Genesis 23:6). He rises and bows down before them instead (Genesis 23:7). Walking away from that offer would be like leaving a warm batch on the cooling rack.

explanations.answer: He gives it to Abraham as a gift
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Ephron says, "I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it." (Genesis 23:11) He says it in front of his own people, with everyone at the city gate listening. That's a big offer said out loud.

explanations.answer: He offers a different cave instead
explanations.explanation: Nice thinking, but Ephron doesn't swap caves. He says, "I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it." (Genesis 23:11) It's the same cave Abraham asked for, and he's giving the field along with it.

No waiting in this scene, friend. Ephron answers right away, and what he says is, "I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it." (Genesis 23:11) His answer comes out fast, with the whole gate listening.

Yes, baker. Ephron says he gives the field and the cave (Genesis 23:11), and Abraham answers, "I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there." (Genesis 23:13) He bows again and keeps asking to pay. That's a man who wants to settle it properly.

Not this time, friend. Ephron really does offer both the field and the cave (Genesis 23:11). Then Abraham says, "I will pay you the price of the field." (Genesis 23:13) He doesn't just take the gift and go.

That's the word, baker. Abraham first asks that Ephron sell it to him "for full price." (Genesis 23:9) Then he "weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver." (Genesis 23:16) No discount, no haggling down.

Not half, friend. Abraham weighs out "the price he had named," which is four hundred shekels of silver (Genesis 23:16). He even asked for it to be sold "for full price." (Genesis 23:9) Shorting a man's silver is not how this goes.

Good try if you thought he was feeling extra generous. But he pays what Ephron named, which is four hundred shekels of silver (Genesis 23:16). Not a shekel over. Full price was what he asked for from the start (Genesis 23:9).

Careful, baker, that one slipped past. The text says Ephron's field, the cave, "and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over to Abraham's possession." (Genesis 23:17-18) So the trees go with the field. Ephron keeps no trees.

Right, baker. The text says the field, the cave, "and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over to Abraham's possession" in front of the Hittites at the gate (Genesis 23:17-18). Trees included. That's one full package, like buying the whole batch and getting every crumb.

explanations.answer: He buries his wife Sarah in the cave
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. "After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre." (Genesis 23:19) All that talking at the gate was about this one thing. Now Sarah has her resting place.

explanations.answer: He gives the field back to Ephron
explanations.explanation: No giving back, friend. The field and the cave were deeded over to Abraham as a burial site (Genesis 23:20). He paid for it, and then he used it. Handing it back would undo the whole deal.

explanations.answer: He builds a city on the field
explanations.explanation: That's a big plan, but it isn't in this passage. The text says Abraham "buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah." (Genesis 23:19) The field was deeded to him "as a burial site." (Genesis 23:20) A burial is what happens there.
